recipe: Kung pao-style chicken with peppers and peanuts
servesNote: 2 portions — 875 kcal / 57 g protein each. ⭐ Thigh fillet deliberately, not breast: it is juicier AND cheaper at Aldi, so there is no trade-off. The peppers are structural components, not a garnish that can be dropped when you are in a hurry.
adaptations: ⛔ THE CORNFLOUR IS OUT AND THIS DISH NEEDS IT TWICE — 2 tsp to velvet the chicken and ~1 tsp to thicken the sauce. Velveting is described in the method as the non-negotiable step, and it is the starch that does the work. Without cornflour this becomes a plain stir-fry with a thin sauce. ⭐ Plain flour will thicken the sauce at a pinch; it will NOT velvet.

⛔ THE TOASTED SESAME OIL IS OUT. It goes in off the heat at the very end as a finishing aroma, so there is no substitute that behaves the same way — leave it out rather than replacing it with plain oil, which adds fat and nothing else.
⛔ THE GINGER & GARLIC PASTE IS OUT, but this recipe already calls for fresh garlic and fresh ginger separately, so just increase those slightly and skip the sachet.

⚠️ SOY IS DOWN TO 4 SACHETS, NO BOTTLE. This wants 2 tbsp (~30 ml) split between the velvet and the sauce — that is the 30 ml Gousto sachet almost exactly, so use it here and keep the 8 g ones for elsewhere.

⛔ NOT A GONG BAO, AND THE CARD WILL NOT PRETEND. Aldi Reading sells neither Sichuan peppercorns nor Chinkiang black vinegar. This takes the Chinese-American branch openly. Balsamic is the closest stand-in for the black vinegar.
⚠️ THIGH FILLETS ARE NOT IN THE HOUSE — Tuesday bought bone-in skin-on thighs and whole legs. Boning out thighs works; allow ten more minutes.

prep: Cut the thighs into EVEN 2 cm cubes — even matters more than small, because unevenly sized pieces cannot all be done at the same moment.

⭐ VELVET. Chicken + 2 tbsp water + 1 tbsp soy in a bowl. Stir and squeeze with your hand ~30 seconds until the liquid has been completely absorbed and the meat looks tacky rather than wet. Then 2 tsp cornflour, the rice wine and 2 tsp oil, mixed until every cube is slicked in a thin gluey coat. Leave 15–20 min. This is the non-negotiable step — the starch sets into a micro-layer that shields the meat from the pan, and the water it absorbed stays inside.
Rinse the rice until the water runs clear and get it cooking.

⛔ MIX THE SAUCE COMPLETELY BEFORE THE PAN GOES ON. Remaining 1 tbsp soy, vinegar, 2 sriracha, sugar, ~1 tsp cornflour, black pepper, 1 tbsp water. Stir until the sugar has dissolved and no cornflour is settled on the bottom. Set it next to the hob.

Line everything else up within arm's reach: peppers, spring onion whites and greens in separate piles, garlic + ginger + chilli powder together, peanuts, sesame oil. ⭐ A stir-fry is 4 minutes of cooking preceded by all the work.

steps.text: Peanuts into your largest pan, dry, medium heat, shaking until they smell toasted and take a shade more colour. Onto a plate. Do this even though they came roasted — it wakes them up, and a plate is where they need to be anyway.

HIGHEST heat, 1 tbsp oil. When it shimmers and moves like water, add HALF the chicken in a single layer and leave it undisturbed until the undersides have set opaque with brown patches (~90 sec). Toss 30–40 sec more until the outsides are coloured but the centres still slightly translucent, and out. Repeat with the second half. ⚠️ If the pan visibly stops sizzling when the chicken goes in, you have added too much.

Last ½ tbsp oil, still high. Peppers + ½ tsp salt. Toss and spread until the edges have blistered and blackened in places but the squares still have a distinct CRUNCH when you bite one. ⛔ They should not soften — charred outside, raw-crisp inside.

⭐ TURN THE HEAT DOWN TO MEDIUM — this matters. Push the peppers aside, garlic + ginger + chilli powder into the clear space, 20–30 seconds, just until fragrant and the garlic is barely pale gold. Do not let them darken. Aromatics burn in seconds at stir-fry heat and burnt garlic makes the whole dish acrid.
Spring onion whites, toss, then all the chicken and its juices back in, heat to high, ~30 seconds until heated through and cooked to the centre.
Stir the sauce again — the cornflour will have settled — and ⭐ pour it around the EDGE of the pan, not into the middle.
Toss constantly 30–60 seconds until the sauce has gone from cloudy to glossy and clings to each piece instead of running to the bottom. Too thick, a tbsp of water; too thin, 20 more seconds.

⭐ OFF THE HEAT ENTIRELY. Sesame oil and the spring onion greens, toss once or twice. Sesame oil goes in off the heat — a finishing oil whose aroma compounds are volatile; cooked, it just tastes flat and slightly burnt.

Peanuts in LAST, right before plating, so they are still fully crunchy. Serve over rice immediately. Maria's next-day lunch: chicken and sauce reheat well and the peppers stay pleasant, but the peanuts go soft overnight — set a handful aside before serving and pack them separately, with the spring onion greens, to add after heating.
